**Defensible v1 – 12‑Hospital Health System Rollout of an AI Sepsis‑Risk CDSS** | Domain | Key Objectives | Practical Steps (v1) | Deliverables / Metrics | |--------|-----------------|----------------------|------------------------| | **Clinical Safety** | • Demonstrate that the tool improves patient outcomes without adding harm.
• Provide continuous monitoring and rapid response to safety signals. | 1. **Pre‑deployment validation** – Run the algorithm on a retrospective cohort from each hospital (≥ 3,000 sepsis cases) to confirm AUC ≥ 0.80 and calibration within ±5 % of observed risk.
2. **Prospective pilot** – Deploy in 2–3 “low‑volume” units (e.g., telemetry, general medicine) for 90 days with a dedicated Clinical Safety Officer (CSO).
3. **Integration & alert logic** – Embed the score as a non‑interruptive flag; set a threshold that triggers an EHR order set for lactate, cultures, and early antibiotics.
4. **Provider training** – 1‑hour live demo + e‑learning module; competency quiz (≥ 85 % pass).
5. **Safety monitoring dashboard** – Real‑time dashboards showing alert volume, override rate, time to antibiotic, ICU admission, mortality.
6. **Adverse event review** – Monthly safety committee reviews any missed sepsis or false‑positive alerts that led to unnecessary antibiotics. | • Validation report (AUC, calibration plots).
• Pilot safety data: alert count, override %, 30‑day mortality vs baseline.
• CSO sign‑off on safety metrics. | | **Legal & Regulatory Exposure** | • Meet HIPAA, FDA/ISO, and institutional risk‑management requirements.
• Protect the system from liability and ensure clear governance of data use. | 1. **Regulatory classification** – Confirm that the tool is a “Software as a Medical Device” (SaMD) under 21 CFR Part 820; obtain FDA pre‑market notification (510(k)) if required, or confirm exemption.
2. **Data governance** – Create a Data Use Agreement (DUA) with the vendor: de‑identified data only for model improvement; no PHI sharing beyond EHR integration.
3. **HIPAA compliance** – Ensure all data flows are encrypted in transit and at rest; audit logs capture access.
4. **Risk management & liability** – Update the hospital’s risk register to include AI‑CDSS; obtain professional liability coverage that covers algorithmic errors.
5. **Informed consent / patient notification** – Add a clause in the EHR “Patient Consent” section: “Your clinical care may be supported by an AI system that assesses sepsis risk.”
6. **Vendor contract clauses** – Indemnification, audit rights, data ownership, and termination for non‑compliance.
7. **Governance board** – Form a cross‑disciplinary AI Oversight Committee (physicians, IT, legal, compliance) to review quarterly performance and policy updates. | • FDA/ISO certification status.
• Signed DUA & vendor contract with liability clauses.
• Updated risk register entry.
• Consent language in EHR. | | **Financial Structure** | • Create a sustainable, transparent cost model that aligns incentives across the 12 hospitals.
• Demonstrate ROI through improved outcomes and reduced costs. | 1. **Subscription pricing** – $2,500 per seat (provider) per year; volume discount: 10 % for > 200 seats.
2. **Capital allocation** – Allocate $300k upfront for integration & training; $100k annual maintenance.
3. **Reimbursement strategy** – Leverage CMS’s Sepsis Bundle QI incentives ($1,000 per episode) and potential future ICD‑10 coding for AI‑assisted diagnosis.
4. **Cost‑benefit analysis** – Model:
• Baseline sepsis mortality 15 % → 30 deaths/yr (12 hospitals).
• Expected reduction 20 % → 6 fewer deaths, saving $1M in ICU days ($150k per death avoided).
• Avoided antibiotic overuse: 10 % of patients → $200k savings.
• Net benefit ≈ $1.4 M vs $3.6 M subscription + integration = ROI > 300 %.
5. **Budgeting & reporting** – Monthly financial dashboard showing spend vs. projected savings; annual audit by external CPA. | • Subscription contract signed with all 12 hospitals.
• Annual budget sheet and ROI projection.
• Financial dashboard (P&L, cost‑savings). | --- ### Step‑by‑Step Rollout Timeline | Week | Activity | |------|----------| | 0–2 | Finalize vendor contract; sign DUA. | | 3–4 | Conduct retrospective validation across all sites. | | 5–6 | Build integration (FHIR APIs, EHR flag). | | 7–8 | Deploy pilot in 2 units; launch CSO and safety dashboard. | | 9–12 | Collect pilot data; run monthly safety review. | | 13 | Adjust alert thresholds if override > 30 %. | | 14–16 | Roll out to remaining hospitals; provide training. | | 17+ | Continuous monitoring, quarterly governance reviews, annual financial reporting. | --- ### Key Risk Mitigation Points 1. **Algorithm Drift** – Re‑train model annually using new data; monitor performance metrics (AUC, calibration). 2. **Alert Fatigue** – Keep override rate < 25 %; if higher, refine threshold or add contextual filters. 3. **Liability** – Ensure the vendor’s indemnification covers false positives that lead to unnecessary antibiotics. 4. **Data Security** – Conduct quarterly penetration tests; maintain SOC‑2 Type II compliance for the vendor. 5. **Regulatory Changes** – Assign a Compliance Officer to track FDA/ISO updates and adjust documentation accordingly. --- ### Bottom Line A defensible v1 for this 12‑hospital system is a tightly scoped, data‑driven pilot that validates clinical benefit, embeds robust safety monitoring, satisfies HIPAA/FDA/ISO requirements, and aligns the financial model with measurable outcome improvements. Once the pilot demonstrates acceptable safety metrics and a positive ROI, the system can be scaled across all hospitals with confidence in its regulatory standing and economic sustainability.
